title: Services Agreement

tracker.notes: EUR 88k. by 15 Oct. Pranav: PipeKit can be reused 'like we did for Northwind'

verdict: Do not sign yet: 3 blocking issues to resolve
escalate: Conflict with a signed commitment and no waiver on file

findings.title: PipeKit reuse: AtliQ assigned PipeKit IP to Northwind — 'sole owner' warranty may be untrue
findings.explanation: Northwind MSA cl. 9.2 vested all IP in the deliverables, 'including any … tools, frameworks, libraries and pre-existing materials incorporated', in Northwind. The Northwind pipeline incorporated PipeKit (SOW-1 S1.2). This draft has AtliQ warrant it is the sole owner of PipeKit and indemnify against breach. Evidence: 6.1 Supplier shall deliver the services using its proprietary data-pipeline accelerator "**PipeKit**", comprising reusable ingestion connectors, transformation templates, data quality rule libraries and orchestration modules. PipeKit shall be incorporated into the Work Results to reduce implementation time and cost. / 6.2 Supplier hereby grants Client a perpetual, irrevocable, non-exclusive, worldwide, royalty-free right to use, reproduce, modify and operate PipeKit as incorporated in the Work Results, for the purposes of operating, maintaining and further developing the Platform, including for the benefit of Client's customers. Client may sub-license this right to its affiliated companies and to service providers acting on its behalf.
findings.suggestion: Before signing: get counsel's view on what Northwind now owns; ask Northwind for a licence-back or confirmation; meanwhile soften the warranty to 'owns or is entitled to license' and cap the related indemnity.
findings.quote: All Intellectual Property Rights in the Deliverables, including any software, tools, frameworks, libraries and pre-existing materials incorporated into the Deliverables, shall vest in the Client absolutely upon payment of the Charges for the relevant Milestone.
findings.precedent: Pranav: 'PipeKit can be reused like we did for Northwind' (tracker C-028). K: 'I skimmed the IP and boilerplate' on Northwind.

findings.explanation: The contract incorporates a document that is not in this draft, so you would be agreeing to terms you have not seen.

findings.quote: 15.5 The following Annexes form part of this Agreement: Annex 1 (Statement of Work), Annex 2 (Milestones and Remuneration), Annex 3 (Data Processing Agreement incl. SCCs).

findings.title: Foreign governing law: Federal Republic of Germany
findings.explanation: Governing law is Federal Republic of Germany. Karandeep's checklist: 'gov law → ours (India for Pvt Ltd, US for Inc)'. AtliQ has no presence there and would have to litigate abroad.
findings.suggestion: Ask for Indian law with Mumbai/Pune arbitration (Pvt Ltd) or a US state (Inc); fall back to a neutral seat such as SIAC/LCIA arbitration.
findings.quote: governed by the laws of Federal Republic of Germany

findings.title: Uncapped only for intent / gross negligence / injury (standard carve-out)
findings.explanation: Looks alarming but is the normal German-law carve-out; the general cap still applies to ordinary negligence.
findings.suggestion: Acceptable; confirm a general cap (e.g. 1x fees) applies to everything else.
findings.quote: 9.1 The Parties shall be liable without limitation for damage caused intentionally or by gross negligence, for injury to life, body or health, and under the Product Liability Act (Produkthaftungsgesetz).

findings.title: Delay clause matches AtliQ's standard
findings.explanation: Capped, milestone-based, client delays excluded: the same position Karandeep negotiated with Acme, Northwind and Trustline.
findings.quote: 8.2 If Supplier is in default with a Milestone for reasons for which it is responsible, Client may claim a contractual penalty (Vertragsstrafe) of 0.5% of the Milestone Fee of the affected Milestone for each full week of delay, up to a maximum of 5% of that Milestone Fee.
findings.precedent: Acme / Northwind / Trustline: 0.5% of milestone per week, cap 5%, client delays excluded.

context_notes.body:
# Internal — contract queue (ad-hoc, 22 Sep)
Present: Karandeep, Bhavin, Dhaval, Jay

Called because three people chased Karandeep on the same morning.

Queue as of today (from Jay's list on the whiteboard):
- Harrington (Dhaval) — $210k, US, their paper — by **1 Oct**
- Lakeshore (Jay) — $64k, US — by **3 Oct**
- BlueOrchid pilot (Jay) — $38k — by **5 Oct**
- Gulf Crown (Bhavin) — $140k, Saudi — by **10 Oct**
- TravelHub (Karandeep) — $52k, Dubai — no date
- Rheinwerk (Bhavin) — €88k, Munich — draft arriving tomorrow, by **15 Oct**
- Sunrise SOW-2 (Dhaval) — $45k — Meera sending this week, wants by **8 Oct**

Discussion:
- Karandeep: reviewing late at night after calls, 10pm onwards. A client-paper MSA takes him 3–4 hrs properly. "Harrington alone is a whole evening and I haven't started."
- Dhaval raised ShopSwift — SOW sat 9 days in July waiting for review, Elena's budget slipped a quarter. "We lost that one to our own queue."
- Volume: Bhavin reckons last year was ~5 contracts/month, this year ~9 (MSAs, SOWs, NDAs, DPAs, amendments). Only Karandeep signs.
- Went through Gulf Crown headline terms. Midway Karandeep stopped: "didn't we sign something with the Dubai hotel people that stops us doing hotels in the Gulf?"
- Nobody could find the Al Noor contract quickly — Dhaval searched the shared drive, not there. Karandeep thinks it's in his email "somewhere".
- Bhavin: "I think that expired, no? It was a 2025 thing." Karandeep not sure.
- Jay: "is there a list of what we've agreed to not do?" — silence.
- Dhaval asked if we should send Harrington to counsel. Karandeep: "it's $210k, but Mehta Rao takes a week." Not decided.
- Bhavin: Gulf Crown can't slip, Faisal has a summit on the 14th.

Karandeep will go through them this weekend.

*(No owner, order of review, or deadline per contract was agreed. The Al Noor contract was not located during the meeting.)*
